concepts.name: Vector Quantity
concepts.simple_definition: A vector quantity is a physical quantity that has both magnitude and direction.
concepts.deep_explanation: Unlike scalars, vectors obey vector addition laws (triangle or parallelogram laws). Examples include force, velocity, and displacement.
concepts.real_example: Driving 50 km/h North is a vector (velocity); driving 50 km/h is a scalar (speed).
concepts.common_confusion: Thinking distance is a vector. Distance is a scalar, while displacement is a vector.
concepts.simple_definition_amharic: ቬክተር መጠን ማለት መጠን (magnitude) እና አቅጣጫ (direction) ያለው አካላዊ መጠን ነው።
concepts.deep_explanation_amharic: ከስኬላር በተለየ፣ ቬክተሮች የቬክተር ድምር ሕጎችን ይከተላሉ። ለምሳሌ ኃይል፣ ፍጥነት እና መፈናቀል የቬክተር መጠኖች ናቸው።
concepts.real_example_amharic: 50 ኪ.ሜ/ሰ በሰሜን አቅጣጫ መንዳት ቬክተር ሲሆን፣ 50 ኪ.ሜ/ሰ ብቻ መንዳት ግን ስኬላር ነው።
concepts.common_confusion_amharic: ርቀትን ቬክተር ነው ብሎ ማሰብ። ርቀት ስኬላር ሲሆን መፈናቀል ግን ቬክተር ነው።

concepts.name: 2 Unit 1 Vector Quantities 1.1 Scalars A
concepts.simple_definition: 2 Unit 1 Vector Quantities 1.1 Scalars and Vectors Exercise 1.1  From what you learnt in grade 9, what do you think are the differences between vectors and scalars? By the end of this section, you should be able to: • deﬁne scalar and vector quantities; • describe the difference between vector and scalar quantities; • list some scalar and vector quantities
